scope: Sections 2–3, equal-prior single-marked phase-oracle search. For every nonempty finite database, normalized initial workspace, oracle-independent gates and projective readout, average Born success up to the first maximum is bounded by the success of the explicit Grover circuit with the same query count.

Sharp sine-squared success upper bound through the first maximum and its attainment by computational-basis marking, uniform preparation and one common diffusion reflection per call. For at least two items the construction gives the sine law at every iteration.
If equal-prior success tends to one, then for every positive ε, all sufficiently large N require at least (π/4−ε)√N queries. The algorithm and workspace may vary with N.
The angle of the square root of average success is at most (2T+1) arcsin(1/√N), via a direct sum over candidate labels, the identity-oracle trajectory and a reflection about the readout sectors.
Hilbert direct-sum geometry, Born mass and reflections used in the upper bound, plus the computational basis, normalized uniform state and explicit Grover iterate used for equality.
